bodyparts3d.why: BodyParts3D axes in millimetres with Z up. The liver’s right lobe (hepatovenous segments V to VIII) and the gallbladder lie at -X, and the ventricular wall and the circumflex artery at +X, so -X is the body’s right. The third and fourth ventricles and the prostate mark the midline from head to pelvis. The BodyParts3D 4.3 readers (biliary, dural, cardiac, thoracic) use the same coordinates: their gallbladder and atrial-wall meshes have exactly the centroids of the 4.0 meshes with the same identifiers.

colonvessels.why: The source surfaces are in LPS millimetres (surfaces.json coordinateSystem), so +X is the body’s left. The splenic artery and vein lie at +X and the portal vein at -X, as the spleen and liver require. The coeliac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery arise from the front of the aorta and mark the midline. They lie close together, so they fix the plane’s position and not its tilt: the plane is x = their mean. The source does not register its two phases to each other; both are in the scanner’s coordinates, and the centroid of every sided venous mesh lies at least 35 mm from this plane.

hra-female.why: Metres, glTF axes. Each bladder mesh has exactly the coordinates of the same region in the HRA united female body (hra-female-pelvis-v1.10), where +X is the body’s left: its left ovary, tubes, ligaments, ureter and ilium lie at +X (docs/model-bindings-20261118). The trigone and the bladder neck mark the midline; the plane is x = their mean.

hra-male.why: Metres, glTF axes. The male bladder has no asymmetrical landmark, and no united male body is stored, so its axes cannot be checked from its own anatomy; its manifest records no independent patient-axis verification. The frame is the convention the female organ of the same HRA release shows: +X is the body’s left. The trigone and the bladder neck mark the midline; the plane is x = their mean.

source_findings: BodyParts3D 4.0, hepatovenous segments VII and VIII: the official table assigns object FJ2409 to segment VII, and objects FJ2823 and FJ2824 to segment VIII. FJ2409 has the bounds of segment VI (FJ2822) to within 0.4 mm, and BodyParts3D 4.3 lists it as segment VI. FJ2823 lies posterior and superior, where segment VII lies, and BodyParts3D 4.3 lists it as segment VII. The atlas is corrected with this change (docs/bodyparts3d-liver-correction-20261119): it builds segment VII from FJ2823 and segment VIII from FJ2824, and no longer delivers FJ2409. The two corrected meshes are bound.

BodyParts3D 4.0, trunk of portal vein: the concept is the class of both portal trunks. The official table assigns it objects FJ3102 and FJ3122, and lists the same objects as the trunk of the left and of the right portal vein. The atlas united them under the class name, which reads as the main portal trunk. It now shows the two trunks under their own names, and the pre-hepatic portal vein (FJ3082) as the main trunk.

BodyParts3D 4.3, common hepatic duct: object FJ3079 spans 84 mm in height and ends 60 mm below the cystic duct, so it holds the common bile duct as well. The source labels no common bile duct. Since 2026-11-24 the reader shows the object in two parts, divided where the cystic duct meets it; a later pass of the same day binds the upper part and leaves the lower part unbound.

BodyParts3D 4.3 biliary objects: six labels have two objects each. Three pairs occupy nearly the same place (cystic duct FJ3080 and FJ4526; medial inferior tributary FJ3103 and FJ5819; caudate tributary FJ1883 and FJ5812). Each object has its own record; a pair is not two independent observations.
The gallbladder and both atrial walls have identical geometry in the BodyParts3D 4.0 atlas and in the 4.3 readers. Each file has its own record, because a different reader delivers it.
HRA bladder: two regions of each organ carry the one label “fundus of urinary bladder”; the node names call them dome and base.
BodyParts3D 4.3 dural objects: the unpaired great cerebral vein is labelled right, and the right superior anastomotic vein objects hold eight and two separate components.
